title: Halo-Halo: Layered Shaved Ice with Sweet Beans, Fruit, Ube and Leche Flan
summary: Layers of sweet bananas, tapioca, red beans and tropical fruits under fluffy shaved ice and evaporated milk, topped with ube, leche flan and ube ice cream.
equipment: blender, food processor or ice shaver

ingredients.item: ripe saba bananas or 1 large ripe plantain, peeled and sliced 1 cm on the diagonal
sweetened red beans (canned adzuki in syrup), drained
kaong (sugar palm fruit) in syrup, red and green, drained
nata de coco in syrup, drained
ripe jackfruit, fresh or from a jar, drained and cut in strips
ube halaya (purple yam jam), homemade or bought

steps.title: Cook the bananas
steps.text: Simmer the banana slices with the brown sugar and 300 ml water for 15-20 min until tender and glossy and the syrup has thickened slightly. Cool, then chill; cold fruit stops the ice melting too fast.

steps.title: Boil the tapioca
steps.text: Boil the pearls in plenty of water for 15-20 min, stirring often so they do not stick, until translucent with no white centre. Rinse under cold water to wash off the starch, then stir into 2 tbsp of the banana syrup.

steps.title: Shave the ice
steps.text: Pulse the ice in short bursts until it looks like fluffy snow rather than chips. Keep it in the freezer until you assemble; fine ice packs better and soaks up the milk.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Divide the bananas with a spoonful of their syrup, the tapioca, red beans, kaong, nata de coco and jackfruit between the 4 glasses, so each is about a third full.

steps.title: Pile on the ice
steps.text: Pack the shaved ice on top up to the rim. Crown each glass with a spoonful of ube halaya, a cube of leche flan and a scoop of ube ice cream.

steps.title: Pour and serve
steps.text: Pour 40 ml evaporated milk down the side of each glass and serve straight away with long spoons. Mix everything together as you eat.

tips: Assemble at the last moment; a common mistake is building the glasses early, which leaves a puddle.
Chill the glasses in the freezer for 10 min first.
Asian grocers sell jars of kaong, nata de coco, sweet beans and jackfruit; drain them well.
Swap the ube ice cream for vanilla or coconut if you cannot find it.
storage: Serve as soon as it is assembled. The cooked bananas and tapioca keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
